sentences.text: At a rally in Montana this October, President Trump told the crowd, "we have very little inflation".

assertions.text: Trump said at his Kalispell, Montana rally that we have very little inflation.

sentences.note: Source title: 'President Trump Delivers Emphatic Remarks at Kalispell, Montana Rally - 10/14/26'.

sentences.text: On CBS News, a politics reporter put it the other way: "inflation is higher than when he took office".

assertions.text: A CBS News politics reporter said inflation is higher than when Trump took office.

quote.text: inflation is higher than when he took office
quote.speaker: CBS News

sentences.note: Context: 'cbs news politics reporter catherine watson joins us'.

sentences.text: Very little, or more than before? Let's put both claims against the government's own price index.

sections.name: question-1
sections.title: How high is inflation right now?

sentences.text: Start with the boldest version: Trump has also said, flatly, "we don't have inflation".

assertions.text: Trump said we don't have inflation.

sentences.note: Source title: 'Trump denies there's inflation'; the context is a rally clip.

sentences.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' September report says otherwise: consumer prices were 3.7 percent higher than a year earlier, and still rising month to month.

assertions.text: The BLS reported that the CPI-U rose 3.7 percent over the 12 months to September 2026 and rose again on a seasonally adjusted basis in September, after rising in August.

sentences.text: So there is inflation. The real argument is whether it's high, and that depends on what you compare it with.
Trump's comparison is the past: "we inherited the worst inflation in history", he told the Montana rally.

assertions.text: Trump said at the Montana rally that his administration inherited the worst inflation in history.

quote.text: we inherited the worst inflation in history
quote.speaker: Trump

sentences.text: These figures can't rank all of history, but the 2022 peak was real: in June 2022 the yearly rate hit 9.1 percent, and today's is less than half of that.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change peaked at 9.1 percent in June 2022 and was 3.7 percent in September 2026, less than half the peak.

sentences.note: 9.1 at L48 (2022-06), 3.7 at L99 (2026-09). 'Can't rank all of history': the series starts in 2019, so 'worst in history' is neither confirmed nor refuted here.

sentences.text: And early this year, the low-inflation case was strong. Of January's reading, the YouTube channel The Right-Wing Populist said it was "the lowest we've had in five years".

assertions.text: The Right-Wing Populist said January CPI was the lowest we've had in five years.

quote.text: the lowest we've had in five years
quote.speaker: The Right-Wing Populist

sentences.note: The remark is undated; the reading it describes is January 2026 (context: 'inflation slowed in january 2026 with the cpi up about 2.4%').

sentences.text: Close enough: the January rate was 2.4 percent, a whisker above the lowest reading since March 2021 and about the pace of early 2020 just before the pandemic.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change was 2.4 percent in January 2026; since March 2021 only April 2025, at 2.3 percent, was lower; in January and February 2020 it was 2.5 and 2.3 percent.

sentences.note: L91 2026-01 2.4; L82 2025-04 2.3 is the only lower reading from L33 (2021-03) on; L19-L20 2020-01 2.5, 2020-02 2.3. 'Early 2020' is the earliest 12-month reading the series has.

sentences.text: By September, that case had gone: the yearly rate was higher than in any month of 2024 or 2025.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change in September 2026 was higher than every monthly reading in 2024 and 2025.

sentences.note: 2024 max 3.5 (L69), 2025 max 3.0 (L79, L87), September 2026 3.7 (L99); October 2025 has no reading (L88).

sentences.text: It was also above the 3.0 percent of January 2025 (the month the administration took office): what he actually inherited, and the comparison CBS was making.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change was 3.0 percent in January 2025 and higher, 3.7 percent, in September 2026.

sentences.note: Like for like: both are the headline 12-month NSA change (L79, L99). The inauguration was January 20, 2025, so January 2025 is the month he took office.

sentences.text: Trump has a shorter window in mind: "we're at 1.7% inflation for the last three months", he told reporters.

assertions.text: Trump told reporters we're at 1.7% inflation for the last three months.

quote.text: we're at 1.7% inflation for the last three months
quote.speaker: Trump

sentences.note: Source title: 'President Trump Holds Press Gaggle Before Flight to Kalispell, Montana Rally - 10/14/26'.

sentences.text: The index says otherwise: from June to September, the seasonally adjusted index ran at a pace of about 4.6 percent a year.

assertions.text: Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose from 332.568 in June to 336.298 in September 2026, an annualized pace of about 4.6 percent.

sentences.note: A three-month change compounded to a yearly pace, so it compares with a yearly rate such as the 1.7. The cumulative three-month rise is about 1.1 percent; not read aloud because a viewer could set it against the 1.7 as if both were three-month figures.

sentences.text: To be fair, slide that window back one month, to end in August, and the pace drops to about 0.2 percent a year, because prices fell in June.

assertions.text: Seasonally adjusted CPI-U went from 333.979 (2026-05) to 334.131 (2026-08), an annualized pace of about 0.2 percent, after a fall of 0.4 percent in June.

sentences.note: Same measure and window length as s15, one month earlier; June -0.4 at L192. Shown so the low reading Trump's side could point to is not dropped.

sentences.text: Pick your window, and you pick your answer.
The Federal Reserve, for its part, said at its September press conference that "for more than five years, inflation has been running above target".

assertions.text: The Federal Reserve said at its September press conference that for more than five years inflation has been running above target.

quote.text: for more than five years, inflation has been running above target
quote.speaker: Federal Reserve

sentences.note: Source: 'FOMC Press Conference, September 16, 2026', channel Federal Reserve.

sentences.text: Its stated goal is 2 percent, and its own officials expect 3.7 percent over 2026 on the price index they forecast, called PCE, short for personal consumption expenditures.

assertions.text: The FOMC's September 2026 statement says inflation remains elevated and names the Committee's 2 percent goal.
qualifications: The sentence says only what the goal is; it does not say how long inflation has been above it (s20 carries the CPI record).

assertions.text: FOMC participants' September 2026 projection for PCE inflation (fourth quarter of the previous year to fourth quarter of 2026) is 3.7 percent, against a longer-run rate of 2.0; PCE inflation is the change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures.
qualifications: A projection, not a reading: 'expect' and 'over 2026' in the sentence.

sentences.note: L9 of the statement gives the 2 percent goal; SEP L25 gives the 2026 PCE median 3.7 (longer run 2.0) and L39 defines PCE and says the projections are Q4-to-Q4. Neither line says the goal is defined on PCE, so the sentence says only that PCE is the index they forecast. The 3.7 here is a PCE projection, not the 3.7 percent CPI reading of s05.

sentences.text: On the consumer price index, the yearly rate hasn't dropped below 2.3 percent in any month with a reading since March 2021.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change has been at least 2.3 percent in every month with a reading from March 2021 through September 2026.
qualifications: The sentence states the CPI record only and says 'on the consumer price index'; it does not claim the FOMC statement or projections cover those years.

sentences.note: Minimum 2.3 at L82 (2025-04); October 2025 has no reading (L88, government shutdown), hence 'with a reading'.

sentences.text: And if the rate does come down, will prices?
Even The Right-Wing Populist says not: "prices are technically expanding, but the actual rate is decreasing".

assertions.text: The Right-Wing Populist said prices are technically expanding, but the actual rate is decreasing.

quote.text: prices are technically expanding, but the actual rate is decreasing
quote.speaker: The Right-Wing Populist

sentences.text: That's what happened after the peak: from January 2023 to September 2024, the yearly rate fell from 6.4 percent to 2.4, while the price level itself rose about 5.4 percent.

assertions.text: From January 2023 to September 2024 the 12-month CPI-U change fell from 6.4 percent to 2.4 percent while the CPI-U level rose from 299.17 to 315.301, about 5.4 percent.

sentences.text: So inflation is not gone, and it is not at its peak. Which leaves the next question: what is pushing it up?

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 3.7 percent over the 12 months to September 2026, so there is inflation.
The 12-month CPI-U change in September 2026 was well below its June 2022 peak.

sentences.note: The answer to question 1 in words, pointing back to s05, s08, s11, s12.

sentences.text: The rate had been easing into the new year; then, from March to May, it climbed to 3.3, 3.8 and 4.2 percent.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change eased from 3.0 percent in September 2025 to 2.4 percent in January and February 2026, then rose to 3.3, 3.8 and 4.2 percent in March, April and May 2026.
qualifications: s27 says the price tables show the jump but do not name its cause.

sentences.text: NBC News said the economy had been "heading towards that number earlier this year", the Fed's target, "but then with the Iran war prices shot up".

assertions.text: NBC News said inflation was heading towards that number earlier this year.

quote.text: heading towards that number earlier this year
quote.speaker: NBC News

assertions.text: NBC News said that with the Iran war prices shot up.

quote.text: but then with the Iran war prices shot up
quote.speaker: NBC News

sentences.note: Context: 'we know the fed's target for inflation is 2% all the way down here ... we were actually heading towards that number'. Wording 'the economy had been' to be tightened to 'inflation had been' if the reviewer prefers.

sentences.text: The price tables confirm the jump, but they don't say what caused it.

assertions.text: The CPI-U series shows the 2026 rise in the 12-month rate but does not name its cause.
qualifications: This sentence is the qualification: the tables do not attribute the rise to the war.

sentences.text: One line in them stands out, though: gasoline's own index leapt 24.9 percent in March alone and kept rising through May before falling back in June, but the tables don't say how much of the overall jump that explains.

assertions.text: The CPI-U gasoline index (NSA) rose 24.9 percent in March 2026, 11.1 percent in April and 8.6 percent in May, then fell 9.7 percent in June.
qualifications: The sentence says the tables do not give gasoline's share of the overall rise; no basket weight is cited.

sentences.note: Monthly changes of the gasoline index, L477-L480 (1-mo % column). No basket weights in the package, so no share of the all-items rise is claimed for March-May; s28's 'over half' is the BLS release's own statement for September only.

sentences.text: September's report is more specific: gasoline rose 9.1 percent in that one month and accounted for over half of the month's whole rise.

assertions.text: BLS reported the gasoline index rose 9.1 percent in September 2026, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase.

sentences.text: But an economist on PBS NewsHour pointed out that "the war in Iran is not causing medical care, dental care, toys, apparel".

assertions.text: An economist on PBS NewsHour said the war in Iran is not causing medical care, dental care, toys, apparel price rises.

quote.text: the war in Iran is not causing medical care, dental care, toys, apparel
quote.speaker: PBS NewsHour

sentences.note: Channel PBS NewsHour; the guest is identified earlier in the transcript as chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union.

sentences.text: The report agrees that it isn't only fuel: used cars, airline fares, medical care and apparel all went up in September.

assertions.text: BLS reported that indexes that increased in September 2026 include used cars and trucks, airline fares, medical care and apparel.
qualifications: s31 says core rose 0.3 percent on the month, the same as August, so the spread is modest.

sentences.text: But the spread is modest: prices outside food and energy, called core, rose 0.3 percent on the month, no faster than in August, and 2.6 percent over the year.

assertions.text: BLS reported the all items less food and energy index rose 0.3 percent in September 2026, as it did in August, and 2.6 percent over the year.
qualifications: This sentence is the qualification: the monthly core rate did not accelerate.

sentences.text: Some economists think the underlying rate is higher. "I think underlying inflation is around 3%", Michael Strain said in June.

assertions.text: Michael Strain said in June, I think underlying inflation is around 3%.

quote.text: I think underlying inflation is around 3%
quote.speaker: Michael Strain

sentences.note: Context: 'we're recording this conversation um on june 30th'. 'Some economists': Strain here, and the PBS economist (d7ck9s169ms) says it is 'more than a gas and oil problem'.

sentences.text: Core has run a little under that all year, between 2.4 and 2.9 percent, and it had slowed from 3.1 percent in the summer of 2025 before ticking back up.

assertions.text: The 12-month core CPI-U change ran between 2.4 and 2.9 percent from January to September 2026, down from 3.1 percent in July and August 2025, and rose to 2.6 percent in September after 2.4 in August.
qualifications: The sentence carries the qualification: 'around three' overstates core slightly, and core did decelerate before rebounding.

sentences.text: Housing runs hotter: the shelter index rose 3.2 percent over the year.

assertions.text: The CPI shelter index rose 3.2 percent over the 12 months to September 2026, faster than the 2.6 percent for all items less food and energy.

sentences.text: And tariffs? Economists at the New York Fed estimate they added around 2.9 percentage points to price growth for the goods they studied, by February 2026.

assertions.text: A New York Fed study estimates tariffs made a cumulative contribution of around 2.9 percentage points to price changes for the goods in its sample by February 2026.
qualifications: s36 says the estimate is relative to less-exposed goods, illustrative, and about the sampled goods only.

sentences.text: They caution that it measures those goods against less-exposed ones, so the number is illustrative, and it doesn't tell us how much of overall inflation tariffs explain.

assertions.text: The study identifies the tariff effect relative to less-exposed goods, says the counterfactual should be read as illustrative of the magnitude for the goods in its sample, and so does not measure tariffs' contribution to overall inflation.
qualifications: This sentence is the qualification for s35.

sentences.text: So in September the biggest single push was gasoline, while core sat a little under Strain's figure, with housing above it.

assertions.text: In September 2026 the gasoline index accounted for over half of the monthly all items increase.
Shelter rose 3.2 percent over the year to September 2026, faster than the 2.6 percent for all items less food and energy.

sentences.note: The answer to question 2, pointing back in words; no figures re-read.

sentences.text: The people quoted here mostly weren't arguing about the numbers; they were arguing about the yardstick.
So when someone tells you inflation is high or low, ask: compared with what, and over which months?
And when you hear the rate is falling, check core, and remember that a slower rate still means prices that are climbing.

assertions.text: A falling inflation rate does not mean falling prices: the CPI-U level kept rising while the 12-month rate fell from January 2023 to September 2024.
